chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan said:
I asked him about henna, so he said: Indeed, the person in ihram may touch it and use it to treat his camel, and it is not considered perfume, and there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: Henna (a plant used for dyeing and medicine)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.بَأْسٌ: Harm or difficulty (in a legal context, meaning permissible)
key_terms.طِيبٍ: Perfume (specifically the type that invalidates ihram if used)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in ihram use henna during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the distinction between henna and aromatic perfumes (*thayb*) that invalidate *ihram*, establishing that henna is permissible for both touching and applying to animals like camels. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition in *ihram* applies specifically to scents used for pleasure or identification, whereas henna is primarily viewed as a dye or medicinal agent, thus exempting it from the strict bans on fragrance.
